newsitem.title: BENIN: Dock strike paralyses Benin port.
newsitem.headline: Dock strike paralyses Benin port.

text.p: Dockers paralysed Benin's main port in Cotonou on Friday with a 24-hour strike aimed at persuading the government to review the way it plans to liberalise the handling of containers there, witnesses said.

The national dockworkers union SYNATRAMAP, representing 3,000 workers who load and unload ships and guard and deliver goods, want the business divided equally between four companies rather than Danish group Maersk taking the lion's share.
The government has decided to end the Benin port handling society SOBEMAP's monopoly in the sector.
The union says it opposes plans to give Maersk Line the right to process 40 percent of the container traffic at a terminal it has built for the purpose.
Under the plan, the remainder of the work will be shared between SOBEMAP, French groups Bollore and Saga, and private operators.
The strike brought the port to a standstill. Six ships were in the port, which serves landlocked Burkina Faso, Niger and Mali to the north and neighbouring Nigeria.
